root_causes: Object reference mismatch: The planner repeatedly attempted Place/Rearrange actions using the name 'sushi mat_0' while the environment feedback indicated that this node name was not present in the graph, leading to failed placement attempts despite the object being physically held.

Failure to complete goal propositions: Only 1/3 task propositions were completed; the spoon_2 object remained on table_21 and was never transported to table_29, and the ramekin_1 was never successfully placed on the entryway table.

Ineffective re-planning: After receiving explicit feedback about the missing node name and partial progress, the system continued to issue similar actions (Rearrange/Place with the same bad object reference) instead of querying/refreshing the scene graph for correct identifiers or adjusting the strategy.

Poor coordination and progression logic: Both agents spent many steps exploring and rearranging in the dining room without transitioning to the entryway table or navigating to spoon_2, resulting in high step count and low progress.

Inadequate termination criteria: The episode ended with only 1/3 propositions satisfied and both sushi_mat_0 and ramekin_1 still in hand, implying the system either misjudged task completion or had an overly generic stopping condition unrelated to the stated task goals.
improvement_suggestions: Implement robust object identity management: after any 'node not present in the graph' feedback, trigger an immediate object re-detection step (e.g., look/scan and list objects currently grasped and on nearby surfaces) and update internal IDs before re-attempting Place/Rearrange.

Add explicit goal-tracking checks: maintain a structured checklist for each task object (picked from original location, transported, placed on target table_29) and prevent task termination until all are satisfied or a clear failure condition is reached.

Enhance re-planning on error feedback: when placement fails due to naming or graph issues, re-plan with alternative tools (e.g., generic PlaceHeldObjectOn[target] or Place[object_in_hand, on, target]) instead of repeating the same failing parameterization.

Improve multi-agent role allocation: assign clear sub-goals (e.g., Agent 0 handles sushi_mat_0 and spoon_2, Agent 1 handles ramekin_1) and coordinate navigation so that at least one agent moves toward the entryway table_29 early, rather than both remaining in the dining room.

Introduce targeted navigation to remaining objects and target table: once sushi_mat_0 and ramekin_1 are grasped, explicitly navigate an agent to table_29, and ensure another navigation to table_21 to pick up spoon_2, rather than generic repeated Explore actions.

Refine stopping conditions and success validation: at the end of an episode, validate that all three objects are actually on table_29 (via perception confirmation) before accepting success; otherwise continue planning or explicitly mark as failure with diagnostics.

Reduce redundant long-running actions: monitor actions like Rearrange that remain 'in progress' over multiple steps and set a timeout/abort with an alternative simpler Place-on-surface strategy if progress is not observed.
overall_assessment: The execution only partially completed the task (1 of 3 objects successfully relocated), with repeated failures around placing the sushi mat due to object identity issues and no progress on moving the spoon, leading to inefficient use of steps and premature termination. Overall coordination and error-recovery behaviors were weak.
task_instruction: Move the sushi mat, ramekin, and spoon from the dining room table to the entryway table.
